text: The Nokia 8110 is a mobile phone released in 1996 and announced on 9 September 1996 as the first device in Nokia's high-end 8000 series. It introduced the first 'slider' form factor, where a sliding cover protected the keypad when carried in a pocket and extended downward during use, bringing the microphone closer to the mouth; opening the cover also answered an incoming call. Its curved design, especially when open, led to it being nicknamed the "banana phone." It was the first Nokia phone to feature a monochrome graphic LCD. Designed for the business market, it was one of the smallest and lightest phones available at 152 grams, with better battery life than its predecessor, the Nokia 2110. It was also the first GSM cellphone to use an ARM processor. The improved 8110i model, launched in March 1997, was the first phone to include the SSMS (Smart SMS) engine. Handsets could be updated OTA (Over The Air) with an intelligent menu structure, enabling simple information input sent via structured text messages to an MT receiver, which could then interpret the data and send a structured response back. Ring tone receiving via SMS was also part of the smart messaging protocol, making the 8110i the first mobile phone to support it. Nokia eventually discontinued Smart messaging in favor of the WAP standard but has not removed smart messaging support from later models. The 8110 and 8110i models were succeeded by the Nokia 8810 in 1998, while the 8146 and 8148 models were succeeded by the Nokia 7110 in 1999. An altered version of the phone was famously featured in the science fiction action film The Matrix (1999), where it was modified with a spring-loaded mechanism—though this feature actually appeared on the Nokia 7110.
